title: PenguinSwap on Creditcoin
summary: Trading on Creditcoin's own DEX, why an action that happens here carries no proof, and why that is not a shortcut.

lessons.title: A DEX on the chain the game lives on
body: PenguinSwap is a decentralised exchange running on Creditcoin testnet. The mechanics will be familiar from any constant-product exchange: pools hold two tokens, a swap trades against the reserve, and liquidity providers earn a share of the fee in return for supplying both sides.

What differs is where it sits relative to Vael. Uniswap and Aave are on Ethereum, a chain Creditcoin cannot see. PenguinSwap is on Creditcoin itself, the same chain QuestASC and your hero already live on.
You need tCTC for gas before anything else. It is the native token of Creditcoin testnet and comes from the faucet in the Creditcoin docs, not from a bridge.

lessons.title: Why a local action needs no proof
body: Everything Vael proves is proved because it happened somewhere Creditcoin cannot see. A swap on Ethereum has to be carried across by a Merkle proof and a continuity proof, because no contract on Creditcoin has any record of an Ethereum block.

A swap on PenguinSwap has no such gap. It is a transaction in a block Creditcoin produced. Asking the Block Prover to prove it would be asking Creditcoin to prove Creditcoin to itself, and waiting minutes for an attestation of a block it already has.

That is a real difference in the trust model and it cuts both ways. Local actions are cheaper and immediate, with no attestation wait. Cross-chain actions are what make the proof machinery necessary, and they are where Vael's central claim, that no backend key can complete a quest, actually gets tested.

lessons.title: How a native quest is settled instead
body: A native quest goes through NativePortal rather than QuestASC. You call it, it pulls your tokens, it performs the swap on PenguinSwap with you as the recipient, and it records the completion, all inside one transaction. There is no moment between the action and the completion in which anyone could make a claim about what you did.

That is why it needs no proof and is still not a shortcut. NativePortal has no privilege to say an action happened; it only has the ability to make one happen, with your tokens, at your instruction. If the swap reverts, the completion reverts with it. If you are not the assigned participant, or you have not accepted the quest, or you send less than the minimum, it reverts before a single token moves.

The two paths cannot be confused. A quest is filed to exactly one of them when it is created, by its action type, and cannot move. QuestASC cannot complete a PenguinSwap quest and NativePortal cannot complete a Sepolia one. Even the events are named differently, QuestProofApplied against NativeActionApplied, so nothing reading the chain can mistake one for the other.

quiz.question: Which chain does PenguinSwap run on?
options: Ethereum mainnet
Ethereum Sepolia
Creditcoin
Both Ethereum and Creditcoin
quiz.why: It is Creditcoin's own DEX, which is exactly what makes it different from Uniswap in Vael's terms.

quiz.question: What do you need before you can trade on Creditcoin testnet?
options: Bridged ETH for gas
tCTC for gas, from the testnet faucet
A wrapped version of your Ethereum balance
A validator to sponsor the transaction
quiz.why: tCTC is the native gas token of Creditcoin testnet and comes from the faucet, not from a bridge.

quiz.question: Why does a PenguinSwap swap not need an Attestcoin proof?
options: Because DEX trades are exempt from verification
Because it happens on Creditcoin, which a Creditcoin contract can read directly
Because the amounts are too small to be worth proving
Because PenguinSwap submits the proof for you
quiz.why: Proofs exist to close the gap between chains. There is no gap when the action is in a block the verifying chain produced.

quiz.question: Which actions can Vael verify today?
options: Any transaction on any chain
Portal check-ins, ERC-20 transfers, Uniswap v3 swaps and Aave v3 supplies and borrows on Ethereum Sepolia, plus PenguinSwap swaps and native wraps on Creditcoin
Only Portal check-ins
Anything on Creditcoin, and nothing elsewhere
quiz.why: The five Sepolia actions each have an adapter registered against the event signature they decode. The two Creditcoin actions need no adapter, because NativePortal performs them.

quiz.question: How does NativePortal settle a Creditcoin-native quest?
options: A backend watches the chain and calls QuestManager once it sees the swap
It performs the swap itself and records the completion in the same transaction
It builds the same Merkle and continuity proofs used for Ethereum
It reads the swap log in a later transaction and attests to it
quiz.why: There is no gap for anyone to make a claim in. The action and the completion succeed together or neither happens, and the tokens come out of your own address.

doQuest.title: Swap on PenguinSwap, Creditcoin testnet
steps: Accept a PenguinSwap quest on the quest board. A native quest anchors to no source height, because the action has not happened yet and will happen inside the completing transaction.
Approve NativePortal to spend the token you are selling. It pulls exactly the amount you name and clears the approval again in the same transaction.
Call swapViaPenguinSwap with the quest id, the pair, the fee tier and your own slippage floor. The router pays the proceeds straight to you; nothing is ever held by Vael.
The reward, the badge, your hero XP and any raid damage all land in that same transaction. There is nothing to submit afterwards and nothing to wait for.
